Article Title: US Department of Homeland Security removes 540-day grace period for immigrants after their work authorisation expires; here's what the new rules say
Article Text:
What the rule says

Why the 540-day extension existed

Who will be affected

USCIS faces large backlog

Legal challenge ahead

The US Department of Homeland Security (DHS) has moved to permanently end a policy that allowed many immigrants to continue working for up to 540 days after their employment authorisation expired while renewal applications were pending, according to a Bloomberg Law report. The final rule, released this week, makes permanent an interim measure introduced last year that scrapped the Biden-era 540-day automatic extension period for certain categories of foreign workers. The change is set to take effect when it is published in the Federal Register on October 14.* The automatic extension of work permits during renewal is eliminated, so workers lose authorization when their permit expires, even if a renewal is pending.* The final rule takes effect when it is published in the Federal Register on Oct. 14.* Foreign workers cannot apply to renew their documents until 180 days before expiration.The extension window was designed to ensure immigrant workers were not pushed out of jobs because of processing delays at US Citizenship and Immigration Services. The agency has since added a number of hurdles under the Trump administration for immigrants to keep or renew their employment authorization.The policy affects several groups of immigrants who rely on Employment Authorisation Documents (EADs), including asylum seekers and spouses of H-1B visa holders on H-4 visas. DHS said the move would enable more frequent vetting of applicants seeking employment authorisation. The agency argues that shorter extension periods allow authorities to conduct updated eligibility and security reviews more regularly.Despite the change, USCIS continues to deal with significant renewal delays.According to agency data cited by Bloomberg Law, more than 432,000 work permit renewal applications had been pending for six months or longer as of June 30. Of those, more than 91,000 applications had been awaiting a decision for over 18 months.At the same time, foreign workers are generally not permitted to file renewal applications more than 180 days before their current work permits expire, limiting their ability to offset lengthy processing times.The policy has already faced legal scrutiny. A group of H-4 visa holders filed a lawsuit against DHS in January, arguing that the agency's decision to end the longer automatic extension period violated the Administrative Procedure Act. Last month, a federal judge in California issued a limited injunction blocking enforcement of the interim rule against the plaintiffs involved in the case. The court found that DHS had not adequately followed procedural requirements and failed to address the reliance interests of affected individuals.
Article Summary: US Department of Homeland Security (DHS) has moved to permanently end a policy that allowed many immigrants to continue working for up to 540 days after their employment authorisation expired. The final rule, released this week, makes permanent an interim measure introduced last year that scrapped the 540-day automatic extension period. The change is set to take effect when it is published in the Federal Register on October 14.

Article Title: US Immigration authority has 10-day deadline on home addresses; says: You may not receive your immigration documents if ...
Article Text:
US Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS)

USCIS warns of missed immigration documents

Online filing encouraged

USPS change is not enough

Special cases

US Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) has reminded immigrants and visa holders in the United States that they must report a change of address within 10 days of moving, warning that failure to do so could result in missed immigration notices and documents. As per the agency, anyone with a pending immigration benefit request should notify USCIS of an address change as soon as possible to ensure they continue receiving correspondence and benefits without delays. The requirement applies to most foreign nationals in the United States, although A and G visa holders and visa waiver visitors are exempt.USCIS also clarified that changing the address within the United States Postal Service (USPS) only is not sufficient as USPS does not update the USCIS records automatically or forward the mail sent by the immigration agency. “Changing your address with the US Postal Service (USPS) will not change your address with USCIS and USPS will not forward your mail from USCIS,” the agency said on its website.As per the warning the applicants who fail to update their address with USCIS could miss out on the important notices, immigration documents or other benefit-related correspondence. USCIS also recommends updating the address information with both immigration agency and postal service.USCIS strongly encourages people to submit address changes through a USCIS online account as soon as they move. The agency says updating online satisfies the legal notification requirement, lets it process the change almost immediately, and removes the need to mail a paper Form AR-11, Alien’s Change of Address Card.People can use the self-service tool in their online account even if they originally filed their case by mail. Those with pending cases must enter the receipt number for each pending benefit request so the new address is applied correctly. Filing the paper Form AR-11 by mail also meets the legal requirement.The agency warns that changing an address with the U.S. Postal Service does not update it with USCIS, and USPS will not forward mail from USCIS. People must update both. USCIS recommends using the USPS ZIP Code lookup tool to enter a full address in the standard format.* Sponsors who are U.S. citizens, nationals or lawful permanent residents and have filed an affidavit of support must submit Form I-865 within 30 days of moving.* Citizens with pending or approved orphan or Hague adoption cases must treat a move as a significant household change and follow separate reporting procedures. Failing to report promptly could delay or negatively affect the adoption.* Applicants in VAWA, T and U visa cases, and those seeking Form I-751 abuse waivers, follow special procedures.* Attorneys, accredited representatives and civil surgeons have their own update processes.* If an approval notice says a petition was forwarded to the State Department’s National Visa Center, applicants must also contact that office.* Petitioners whose beneficiary moves should contact the USCIS Contact Center or the office handling the case.
Article Summary: US Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) has reminded immigrants and visa holders in the United States that they must report a change of address within 10 days of moving. Failure to do so could result in missed immigration notices and documents. USCIS strongly encourages people to submit address changes through a USCIS online account as soon as they move.

Article Title: A New York town once known for IBM is resisting a 1-gigawatt AI data centre; residents fear the cost of powering it
Article Text:
AI generated image for representation

East Fishkill imposes a three-year moratorium on data centres

“I just think that we’re at this moment where things are happening very quickly; we need to get our ducks in a row and think about the various ways in which data centres and new energy usage will affect our long-term community cohesiveness, environmental quality, and character,”

Why the proposed 1-gigawatt AI data centre has raised concerns

“The pushback is really to the size,”

“The Treetop center would be 1,000 megawatts. People do not want to pay higher electricity rates because of a larger data centre coming in and putting pressure on the grid.”

“It’s not going to provide work to keep people here like the previous tech businesses did,”

“So what’s the benefit to the town?”

IBM's legacy shapes opposition to the development

Developer challenges the town's data centre ban

New York’s East Fishkill is debating AI infrastructure. The town, located about 70 miles north of New York City, was once a major semiconductor manufacturing hub, with IBM operating a 460-acre campus there for nearly 50 years. However, a proposed 1-gigawatt artificial intelligence (AI) data centre has prompted residents to question whether the project would benefit the community or put additional pressure on its electricity supply.The data center developer Treetop Companies is exploring plans for a facility spanning more than 1 million square feet across approximately 143 acres. Residents have organised protests and pushed for restrictions, arguing the project could raise electricity costs, harm the environment, and offer limited long-term employment.East Fishkill's town board unanimously adopted a three-year moratorium in late June 2026, preventing the consideration of new data centres larger than 20 megawatts until July 2029. Officials said the pause would give the community time to study the potential effects of such facilities on water resources, local ecosystems and the area's character.The opposition gathered momentum even before the developer submitted a formal data centre application to the town. Residents attended public meetings, organised rallies and called for restrictions on large-scale projects.said East Fishkill resident and professor Tanya Radford.The proposed development has also drawn attention because of its expected electricity demand. Residents fear that adding a facility of this scale could strain the grid and raise power bills.The controversy began after Treetop Development purchased property in East Fishkill while initially pursuing approvals for a warehouse project. Residents later discovered that Donovan Drive Holdings, a local property owner associated with the development, submitted a request to the New York Independent System Operator's (NYISO) interconnection queue for about 1,000 megawatts of electrical service.NYISO manages New York's high-voltage electricity grid and reviews requests from large projects seeking to connect to it. The request raised concerns because a 1-gigawatt data centre would consume more electricity than the entire city of Buffalo, which has approximately 275,000 residents. East Fishkill, meanwhile, has a population of around 30,000.Fran Caracappa, a resident and county legislature candidate, said the project's scale was central to the opposition.resident Fran Caracappa, a candidate for county legislature, said.Residents have also questioned whether the facility would create enough permanent jobs to justify its electricity demand and land use.Caracappa said.East Fishkill's resistance comes despite its history as a technology centre. IBM's semiconductor operations employed thousands of workers and helped establish the region's industrial identity. Parts of the former IBM campus now form iPark 84, a mixed-use development that houses commercial, residential and technology facilities.Residents have made it clear that they oppose not technology itself, but the size of the proposed project and its potential impact. The industrial past of the region has raised concerns about contamination of groundwater from semiconductor manufacture . There are still several polluted Superfund sites in the area .Other issues residents raised include noise, diesel backup generators, wetlands, property values, and the loss of the area's rural character.Treetop has appealed the moratorium. In a 17-page objection letter submitted to the town board, the company's attorneys argued that the measure unlawfully targets its property and effectively amounts to a permanent prohibition rather than a temporary planning measure.The company said it had spent years and significant resources advancing development plans, including environmental reviews, wetlands investigations, traffic studies and utility coordination.However, the town’s officials have maintained that no formal data centre application has been submitted and that the moratorium will allow them to assess how local zoning should address large-scale facilities.
Article Summary: East Fishkill imposes a three-year moratorium on data centres. The data center developer Treetop Companies is exploring plans for a facility spanning more than 1 million square feet across approximately 143 acres. Residents have organised protests and pushed for restrictions, arguing the project could raise electricity costs.

Article Title: US Department of Energy declares Power Grid Emergency in 13 States: What it is, and what it means for the residents of the states impacted
Article Text:
Power plant (Representational image)

Why the emergency order has been issued

What it means for residents in impacted US states

NERC Reliability Standard EOP-011-4 addresses Emergency Operations. Requirement 2 provides that “[e]ach Balancing Authority shall develop, maintain, and implement one or more Reliability Coordinator-reviewed Operating Plan(s) to mitigate Capacity Emergencies and Energy Emergencies within its Balancing Authority Area.”

Balancing Authorities are responsible for requesting that their respective Reliability Coordinators issue an EEA in accordance with Requirement 2 and Attachment 1 to Reliability Standard EOP-011-4. Among other things, Requirement 2.2.4 of this reliability standard authorizes Balancing Authorities to make “[p]ublic appeals for voluntary Load reductions.”

Moreover, section 2.2.9 requires Balancing Authority Operating plans to include provisions for “Transmission Operators to implement operator-controlled manual Load shedding, undervoltage Load shedding, or underfrequency Load shedding,” and section 2.2.10 requires such plans to determine reliability impacts of “extreme weather conditions.”

US Secretary of Energy Chris Wright has issued an emergency order authorising PJM Interconnection, the regional transmission operator serving much of the Mid-Atlantic and Midwest regions, to run designated power generation units as needed to protect grid stability. The federal directive, issued on October 12, grants PJM temporary emergency authority running from October 13 through October 16. Under the order, the grid operator can mandate certain power plants to generate electricity and, in limited circumstances, tap into backup power reserves to maintain a steady flow of energy across its multistate network, as per the order available on the department’s official website. Federal officials and grid managers clarified that the order is designed specifically to prevent power interruptions and not to announce scheduled blackouts.Headquartered in the Philadelphia area, PJM Interconnection coordinates wholesale electricity movement across all or parts of 13 states and the District of Columbia.“PJM serves as the Reliability Coordinator and Balancing Authority for its region and is, therefore, responsible for overseeing the dispatch of generation to meet system demand at all times within the limits of the transmission system.The PJM Region includes all or parts of Delaware, Illinois, Indiana, Kentucky, Maryland, Michigan, New Jersey, North Carolina, Ohio, Pennsylvania, Tennessee, Virginia, West Virginia, and the District of Columbia,” the order says.Ahead of strained conditions, the operator issued a Maximum Generation Alert and a Load Management Alert for October 13, pointing to a confluence of weather and scheduled infrastructure downtime. Due to ‘unseasonably warm autumn weather’, forecasted electricity demand is expected to reach approximately 111,500 megawatts or higher on October 13.The second reason is the maintenance window. The grid is currently in its standard seasonal outage cycle, which runs from mid-September through early December. During this period, utilities routinely take generation units and power lines offline for maintenance and upgrades to ensure peak availability ahead of freezing winter weather.Scheduled transmission line outages have restricted the volume of electricity that can be transferred between different zones on the system.According to the Department of Energy (DOE), without emergency federal intervention, PJM faced conditions where it might have had to reduce or cut power service to keep the regional grid balanced."It is our understanding that PJM seeks to unlock and deploy backup generation resources (whether auxiliary, standby, directly-connected, battery storage, or other, and whether synchronized or not to the bulk-power system) at data centers (including, but not limited to, hyperscaler facilities) and at other large load industrial and commercial customer sites as another tool to mitigate any undue risk to the bulk-power system," the order noted.While PJM emphasised that the initial alert does not require immediate mandatory action from household customers, the operational strain could bring voluntary conservation measures into play. Day-to-day electricity usage remains normal, and the emergency declaration is aimed at coordinating power plants to keep systems stable.PJM has, however, issued capacity advisories and has the option to activate demand response initiatives. If conditions tighten, businesses and residents across the 13-state footprint could be asked to voluntarily dial back non-essential power consumption during peak hours.These procedures align with North American Electric Reliability Corporation (NERC) Reliability Standard EOP-011-4, which governs emergency operations. Under these standards, balancing authorities must maintain plans to handle capacity shortfalls and extreme weather impacts.
Article Summary: US Secretary of Energy Chris Wright has issued an emergency order authorising PJM Interconnection, the regional transmission operator serving much of the Mid- Atlantic and Midwest regions. The order grants PJM temporary emergency authority running from October 13 through October 16. Under the order, the grid operator can mandate certain power plants to generate electricity and, in limited circumstances, tap into backup power reserves.

Article Title: Bumble is off the market, agrees to go private in $1.3 billion deal
Article Text:
A $1.3 billion match for Bumble (Picture: Reuters)

Why Bumble decided it was time to sell

Bumble's new co-CEOs are counting on AI to bring daters back

Bumble is going private. The dating app has agreed to be acquired by Ithaca Holdings in a $1.3 billion deal, and Ithaca co-founders Ravi Gupta and John Hegeman will become Bumble's co-CEOs once it closes. Founder Whitney Wolfe Herd, who started the app 12 years ago, will stay actively involved, though her exact role hasn't been spelled out.Ithaca is paying $6.05 per share, a 122.4% premium to Bumble's closing price on June 24, the day before reports emerged that the company was exploring a sale. Investors liked what they saw. The stock jumped 50% on Monday as news of the deal spread and rose another 56% to $5.95 in early trading on Tuesday. Even so, Bumble was worth only about $582 million at Monday's close, far below the roughly $14 billion valuation it fetched on its Nasdaq debut in 2021.An independent committee of Bumble's board recommended the deal after a review of strategic options, and Wolfe Herd stayed out of the discussions and the vote. Blackstone, which owns about 14% of Bumble, has signed off alongside her, giving the deal the shareholder approval it needs.The reasons for selling are in the numbers. Bumble's second-quarter revenue fell 15.2% year-on-year to $211 million, while paying users dropped 16.4% to around 3.2 million. Revenue has been sliding for close to two years, and the company has turned an annual pre-tax profit only once since going public. Last year, it cut nearly a third of its workforce.Gupta held C-suite roles at Instacart before becoming a partner at Sequoia, and Hegeman was previously Meta's chief revenue officer. They will be the first men to lead the women-first app since it listed. The pair described the acquisition as "a bet on the future of humanity", with Ithaca focused on building businesses for a world reshaped by AI.Bumble was already moving that way. Since Wolfe Herd returned as CEO in March 2025, it has added AI help for profiles and messages, started testing an AI matchmaking assistant and introduced Plans in July, which nudges users towards real-world meetups. In August, it scrapped the rule that only women could message first, the very feature that built the brand. Wolfe Herd has also teased a new way to interact that could eventually replace swiping.Rival Match Group, which owns Tinder and Hinge, has also slumped from its 2021 highs, but Hinge keeps pulling in people after serious relationships. Away from public markets, Bumble now gets time to prove it can win those daters back.
Article Summary: Ithaca is paying $6.05 per share, a 122.4% premium to Bumble's closing price on June 24. Founder Whitney Wolfe Herd, who started the app 12 years ago, will stay actively involved, though her exact role hasn't been spelled out. The company has turned an annual pre-tax profit only once since going public.

Article Title: Godfather of AI Yann LeCun opposes Dario Amodei’s call of slowing down AI development, says ‘Anthropic is trying to scare governments by saying…’
Article Text:
Yann LeCun opposes Anthropic: ‘No different from anti-enlightenment’

Yann LeCun, Turing Award winner and widely recognised as one of the three “godfathers of AI,” has pushed back against calls to slow down artificial intelligence (AI) development, accusing Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei of using alarmist messaging to lobby regulators and restrict public access to the technology. Speaking during an interview on the morning of October 12 at the Westin Chosun Seoul in Jung-gu, the co-founder and chairman of AMI Labs addressed the intensifying divide across Silicon Valley over safety regulations and model releases.“It’s natural for companies to release products with safety measures to prevent harm to people,” said LeCun, who won the 2018 Turing Award alongside Yoshua Bengio and Geoffrey Hinton for pioneering the foundations of computer vision and image recognition, was in South Korea for the Industrial AI Global Cooperation Meeting ahead of the IIAC 2026 conference in Tokyo.“However, large language models (LLMs) are difficult to fine-tune, so they can potentially harm humans in certain cases. Sam Altman says, ‘We’ll release them cautiously,’ while Dario Amodei argues, ‘They’re too dangerous to manage and shouldn’t be given to the public.’ I oppose Dario’s view,” he added, as per a report in South Korean publication Chosun.LeCun compared attempts to gatekeep underlying model weights to historical efforts to suppress information.“Restricting access is no different from anti-enlightenment – like the Ottoman Empire banning printing in the 15th century to prevent information from reaching people. Ultimately, foundational AI models should be open-source. Only then can human culture, knowledge, and information spread.”When asked whether modern systems can be controlled, LeCun dismissed the notion that today’s large language models pose an existential threat to society. Instead, he framed alarmist narratives as political leverage.“I don’t think current AI is dangerous. The argument for slowing down AI development is a form of marketing or lobbying. Anthropic is portraying AI as extremely dangerous to scare governments. But LLMs aren’t at that level yet.”While talking about the Hugging Face incident, where an OpenAI model attempted to break out of its environment, LeCun argued that such occurrences stem from poor supervision rather than machine malice.“The Hugging Face incident happened due to intentional or incompetent design flaws. Human supervisors failed to properly design the experimental environment, causing AI agents to deviate. Since these agents aren’t inherently malicious, no harm occurred.”Later during the meeting, LeCun reiterated that governing artificial intelligence is fundamentally a technical challenge rather than a crisis of control.
Article Summary: Yann LeCun says Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei is using alarmist messaging to lobby regulators and restrict public access to the technology. He was in South Korea for the Industrial AI Global Cooperation Meeting ahead of the IIAC 2026 conference in Tokyo.

Article Title: Workday announces new AI agents, Sana experience and C1.ai acquisition at Rising 2026 event
Article Text:
Workday to acquire C1.ai for agentic identity management

Sana becomes the new Workday Home with AI agents

Workday launches Autopilot Agents across HR, finance and IT

Trusted Agent Platform gets headless access

New tools target recruitment and business decisions

Workday expands Anthropic partnership and brings Sana to other platforms

Workday has announced a series of AI updates at its Rising 2026 event. The enterprise software company has signed a definitive agreement to acquire C1.ai, an agentic identity management platform, and introduced new AI agents designed to handle tasks across human resources (HR), finance, and IT. The announcements also include a redesigned Workday Home powered by Sana, a platform that lets customers build and manage their own AI agents, along with new tools for workforce planning and financial decisions.Workday is also expanding its partnerships with Anthropic and other technology companies to bring its AI capabilities into the tools employees already use. The updates reflect the company's push to move AI beyond answering questions towards completing business tasks.Workday has signed a definitive agreement to acquire C1.ai, a platform focused on identity management for people and AI agents. The acquisition is intended to help Workday manage access to applications, data and systems for employees and AI agents throughout their lifecycle.With the acquisition, Workday aims to establish an identity governance layer covering people, money and agents. The system is designed to ensure employees and AI agents receive the right access permissions when they join an organisation, change roles, or leave.The move comes as businesses increasingly deploy AI agents to perform tasks across enterprise systems, creating a need to manage their access and permissions alongside those of human employees.Workday has introduced Sana as the new Workday Home, describing it as an agentic experience designed to complete tasks rather than simply answer questions.Employees can make requests in natural language, and Sana coordinates the relevant Workday AI agents to carry out the requested actions. The company said Sana Concierge can handle HR and IT requests, including employee onboarding and password resets, before they become support tickets.Workday is positioning Sana as an interface that lets employees access business services and get work done without navigating multiple systems or manually completing every step.Workday has also launched Autopilot Agents that operate in the background across HR, finance and IT. The agents are designed to handle tasks involving hiring, payroll, accounting and compliance.According to the company, the agents can identify work that needs attention and recommend actions or take them within customer-defined policies and approval limits. Sana coordinates their activities, while existing business rules determine what they can do independently.The objective is to reduce the time employees spend on routine operational tasks, allowing teams to focus on decisions that require human judgement.Workday's Trusted Agent Platform now supports headless access to HR and finance capabilities, allowing customers to build, run and govern their own AI agents.The company said Agent-Ready Tools, Agent Harness, Developer Agent, Custom Agents and Data Cloud are generally available. These capabilities support different AI models and development frameworks.Workday, customer-built and partner-developed agents operate under the same permissions, approval processes and audit trails, according to the company. The approach is intended to give organisations flexibility in developing AI agents while retaining governance over how they access and use business data.Workday has announced additional features for recruitment, workforce planning and financial analysis. The new Candidate Profile feature allows job seekers to save their information once and reuse it when applying to companies that use Workday for recruitment. The company aims to reduce friction in the application process and address an estimated application-abandonment rate of around 60%.Workday Decision Intelligence is now available across the company's portfolio. The AI-powered HR and finance analyst helps teams model scenarios using live, governed Workday data. Businesses can compare hiring strategies, identify skills gaps and analyse financial variances before routing recommendations through existing approval processes.Workday has also introduced Work Intelligence, which helps organisations break jobs into individual tasks and map them to the skills required to perform them. Using Workday Skills Cloud's database of more than 75,000 skills, the tool helps leaders determine which tasks AI can automate, which it can support, and which should remain with people.Workday and Anthropic have announced a partnership connecting Claude's reasoning capabilities with Sana AI agents and Workday's business data and context. Depending on the task, users can access the experience through Sana or Claude.Workday is also expanding Sana's availability beyond its own platform. The agentic experience and orchestration engine will work within tools employees already use, including Claude, Google Cloud's Gemini Enterprise, Microsoft Copilot, Microsoft Teams and Slack. The integrations let employees access Workday capabilities through existing workplace tools rather than switching between applications.
Article Summary: Workday has signed a definitive agreement to acquire C1.ai, an agentic identity management platform. The company has introduced new AI agents designed to handle tasks across human resources (HR), finance, and IT. Workday is also expanding its partnerships with Anthropic and other technology companies to bring its AI capabilities into the tools employees already use.

Article Title: Microsoft has bought more than 600 acres in an Iowa town of about 1,300 people for a proposed data center; more than 200 residents packed a school meeting as the company outlined roads, utilities and
Article Text:
Representative Image

How Microsoft’s purchase of more than 600 acres in Woodward sets the stage for a data center

What Microsoft told more than 200 residents about roads, utilities and electricity

Why Woodward residents questioned the lack of community involvement

“Is this something that we get a vote on? I mean, something this big, the community should get to vote on instead of doing back-end deals,”

“I can safely say I have not seen a single one of you at a budget meeting when we try to balance a budget for this community,”

“We have to find revenue sources for our community.”

Why the residents-only meeting drew criticism over public access

“It runs counter to the openness that the public meetings all guarantee,”

“From my vantage point, it erodes the trust and confidence, and the respect for Woodward city government.”

A proposed Microsoft data center in a small town in Iowa may have triggered concerns over the area’s future. The tech giant has reportedly purchased more than 600 acres of industrially zoned land in Iowa’s Woodward community last week. This sets the stage for a potential development that could reshape the town's tax base and infrastructure.According to a KCCI report, more than 200 residents gathered at Woodward-Granger High School this week to hear Microsoft representatives and Mayor Todd Folkerts explain preliminary plans, including roads, water and sewer upgrades, and electricity arrangements. The meeting also exposed residents’ concerns about limited community involvement, environmental effects of the planned data centre, and whether a project of this scale should require a public vote.Microsoft completed the purchase of approximately 600 acres in the Woodward Eco Business Park last week, the report noted. The property was acquired from an independent seller rather than the city and is already zoned for industrial use, which permits data center development.The business park received certified-site status in 2018, making it a potential location for industrial projects.However, Microsoft has not yet designed the proposed data center, and company representatives said the design process could take roughly two years before construction could begin.The project would be located on the southern side of Woodward, a community of approximately 1,300 people. Its scale has raised questions about how the development would affect the town’s infrastructure, environment and quality of life.Microsoft representatives met with Folkerts for a 90-minute session at Woodward-Granger High School on Monday. The session brought residents and company officials together to discuss the proposal and answer questions about its potential impact.The company said it would pay for the infrastructure required for the project, including road construction and paving, water and sewer upgrades, and electricity infrastructure. Government Affairs Infrastructure Director Cloteal LaBroi said the company’s plans would also include arrangements designed to limit the project's impact on existing municipal services.Microsoft said a closed-loop cooling system would not affect the city's water resources. It also plans to buy electricity directly from a wholesaler, which representatives said would keep the project from affecting the local power grid or raising electricity rates for residents.Company officials said the data center would create dozens of jobs and contribute to the town’s tax base. However, the facility’s final design and construction timeline remain uncertain.Though Microsoft assured infrastructure and economic benefits, some residents seemed frustrated with the land-acquisition process. Some asked whether town residents had a right to speak on an issue that might have a huge impact on their lives.one resident said.Folkerts responded that residents would not vote directly on the proposal. Instead, the city council would vote on negotiations between Microsoft and the city, and the council would have to approve a development agreement before the project could move forward. The council would also need to approve a site plan later.Defending the need to find additional revenue for the town, Folkerts told the gathering:he said to the crowd.The meeting also attracted criticism over restrictions on who could attend. It replaced the city's regular council meeting but was limited to Woodward residents, who had to show proof of residency to enter. Several people were turned away.Randy Evans, president of Iowa’s Freedom of Information Council, was among those denied entry. He questioned whether the restriction was consistent with Iowa's open meeting laws.Evans told KCCI.Tensions also surfaced inside the auditorium, where police escorted out a vocal opponent after an altercation during the meeting. Outside, about half a dozen protesters gathered to oppose data center developments, including projects proposed in Ames and Boone.
Article Summary: Microsoft has reportedly purchased more than 600 acres of industrially zoned land in Iowa’s Woodward community. This sets the stage for a potential development that could reshape the town's tax base and infrastructure. More than 200 residents gathered at Woodward-Granger High School this week to hear Microsoft representatives and Mayor Todd Folkerts explain preliminary plans.

Article Title: Chinese companies 'once again tell' America: You can not keep Nvidia away from us
Article Text:
Representative Image

Chinese companies turn to Nvidia chips amid AI computing shortage

“We believe China’s AI compute expansion has so far been constrained less by demand than by availability of high-end compute,”

“China’s domestic makers of workstation chips and cards have experienced unprecedented growth since 2022.

US firms continue to be restricted by a combination of outdated US export controls, which cover gaming products released nearly a half a decade ago, and China’s own limits on US imports.”

Nvidia's CUDA software remains a factor for Chinese companies

China's AI spending adds pressure on chip supplies

“There is a consensus across the industry that the current shortage in AI compute will not be resolved until at least 2030,”

Nvidia looks to retain its position in China

“Regulators are talking with tech companies to find out if their demand for Nvidia’s RTX 5500 is necessary,”

“The honest conclusion will be ‘yes’.”

Nvidia still seems to be central to China's artificial intelligence (AI) ambitions. Despite years of US export restrictions aimed at limiting China's access to advanced AI processors, Chinese tech companies have reportedly bought more than 1 million Nvidia gaming and workstation chips this year to address a growing computing-power shortage.According to a report by The Financial Times, Chinese companies are now turning to Nvidia products that comply with US export controls, even as they work to build alternatives that could eventually reduce their reliance on the American chipmaker. The purchases highlight how difficult it has been for Beijing to reduce its dependence on American technology while rapidly expanding its AI infrastructure. Chinese chipmakers, including Huawei, Alibaba, Baidu and Cambricon, are increasing production, but supply has struggled to keep pace with demand from technology companies developing AI models and data centres.The report cited industry insiders, who said Chinese technology companies have purchased more than 1 million Nvidia gaming and workstation processors this year. The chips include the RTX Pro 6000D, RTX Pro 5000 and RTX 5090, which were not designed specifically for advanced AI workloads but can be repurposed for certain computing tasks.The shortage has emerged as China accelerates its efforts to develop domestic alternatives to American AI hardware.Industry insiders estimate that available AI chip supply could reach 3.5 million units this year, including around 1 million manufactured overseas. However, total demand is expected to exceed 5 million units.said Gary Yu, a Morgan Stanley analyst based in Hong Kong.Nvidia said,Beyond hardware availability, Nvidia's CUDA software platform is another reason Chinese tech companies keep seeking its processors. CUDA lets developers use graphics processing units for general computing tasks and has become a standard part of many AI development workflows.Chinese companies are being encouraged to move towards domestic alternatives, including Huawei's CANN software platform. However, transitioning existing systems and workflows to a different software ecosystem presents challenges.DeepSeek is working with Huawei to improve its hardware and software capabilities, while Huawei is also using AI tools to accelerate the migration of programming code from CUDA to CANN.Meanwhile, Chinese companies are investing in domestic processors. Huawei is expected to produce 1.6 million AI chips this year, while Alibaba and Baidu's chip divisions are expected to manufacture a combined 1 million units. Cambricon is projected to produce around 300,000 chips, according to people familiar with the companies' plans.Alibaba recently introduced its Zhenwu V900 processor, while Huawei is developing large computing clusters that connect multiple processors to compensate for performance differences between individual chips.The demand for computing power has increased as Alibaba, ByteDance and Tencent invest in AI models, data centres and agentic AI tools. Their combined capital expenditure this year could more than double to approximately RMB 700 billion, or $104 billion, according to people familiar with the matter.Alibaba chief executive Eddie Wu said during the company's August earnings call.The shortage is also prompting Chinese AI developers to secure computing capacity overseas. Tencent has signed an agreement with Oracle to lease 100,000 GPUs across data centres in Southeast Asia, while ByteDance and Alibaba are pursuing similar arrangements, according to the report.These overseas facilities use Nvidia's advanced processors, including the B300, giving Chinese companies access to computing resources that remain hard to obtain domestically.Nvidia is preparing another workstation processor, the RTX Pro 5500, which is expected to offer higher performance than its existing products available in China. According to two people familiar with the move, Chinese companies have already indicated orders exceeding 2 million units, with shipments potentially beginning towards the end of this year. However, Chinese regulators are examining whether demand for the processor is justified.said one executive at a leading Chinese technology company.The developments underline the challenge facing both Washington and Beijing. US restrictions aim to limit China's access to advanced computing technology, while Beijing works to build a self-sufficient chip industry. Yet rising AI demand and the continued importance of Nvidia's hardware and software show why Chinese tech companies haven't been able to move away from the American chipmaker as quickly as intended.
Article Summary: Chinese companies turn to Nvidia chips amid AI computing shortage. shortage has emerged as China accelerates its efforts to develop domestic alternatives to American AI hardware. Industry insiders estimate that available AI chip supply could reach 3.5 million units this year. However, total demand is expected to exceed 5 million units.

Article Title: How hackers took control of hundreds of refrigerators in supermarkets across France, raising the temperature to 50 degree celsius sparking fires and spoiling food
Article Text:
France supermarket cyberattack: Hackers turn refrigerators into ovens, heating them to 50°C, spoiling food at hundreds of stores

How hackers took control of freezers in France

Cyberattacks are moving well beyond stealing email account passwords, corporate data breaches and compromising smartphones. A wave of cyberattacks have impacted people’s dinner tables in France. Media reports pouring in from the country say that the Paris prosecutor’s office has launched an investigation following an overnight cyberattack that seized remote control of commercial refrigeration and freezer units across hundreds of French supermarkets. By overriding internal heating controls, attackers forced temperatures up to 50°C (122°F), triggering small fires, melting cooling equipment and destroying vast stockpiles of perishable food.French retail giant Les Mousquetaires, which operates the Intermarché and Netto supermarket chains, confirmed that damages will reach several million euros, while Intermarché CEO Thierry Cotillard told broadcaster BFM-TV that the incident triggered losses totaling “tens of millions of euros nationwide in a single day.”“Targeting equipment essential to the preservation of fresh products and to the food supply of the French people is of extreme gravity and is unprecedented,” Dominique Schelcher, CEO of French grocery chain Coopérative U, wrote in a statement on X.According to BFM-TV, the hackers remotely executed forced, continuous defrost cycles across impacted grocery locations. Rather than maintaining freezing conditions, systems were dialed up to 50°C. According to reporting from Le Monde, attackers also manipulated safety parameters by extending defrost cycles inside freezers and cold rooms from the standard one-hour duration up to eight hours, a deliberate step designed to suppress and delay automated alarm systems.Supermarkets deploy centralised industrial control panels to govern multiple refrigeration lines, often connecting them directly to the internet so external contractors can run diagnostics and maintenance remotely.The French government warned that exposing industrial management dashboards to the public internet violates cybersecurity best practices, stating that remote access should always be strictly cordoned off behind trusted IP addresses.An alert issued by France’s National Cybersecurity Agency (ANSSI) revealed that the attackers targeted two specific refrigeration controller models manufactured by Danish industrial group Danfoss: the AK-SC and AK-SM series.In response, Danfoss acknowledged that it was aware of the disruptions in France, maintaining that the incident was isolated to units operating unpatched code.“The affected units were running outdated firmware,” Danfoss stated, noting that it has “long advised customers to keep supported systems updated with the latest firmware and to migrate legacy systems to current-generation solutions.”
Article Summary: Hackers seized remote control of commercial refrigeration and freezer units across hundreds of French supermarkets. By overriding internal heating controls, attackers forced temperatures up to 50°C (122°F) French retail giant Les Mousquetaires, which operates the Intermarché and Netto supermarket chains, confirmed that damages will reach several million euros.

Article Title: Intel's former CEO Pat Gelsinger has a 'message' for OpenAI, Amazon, Anthropic, Tesla, Microsoft and other companies: Your AI chips 'cannot' solve AI's biggest shortage as …
Article Text:
1) Silicon still takes quarters to manufacture, no matter how fast we design

2) Memory bandwidth and advanced packaging are huge choke points

3) Copper is giving way to optical

4) Energy capacity is becoming economic capacity

I also think today's explosion of specialized

AI chips

will consolidate around fewer architectures.

Where AI helps in chip design, and where it falls flat

As technology heavyweights including OpenAI, Amazon, Anthropic, Tesla, Google and Microsoft pour massive resources into custom in-house processors, former Intel CEO Pat Gelsinger has offered a reality check: designing specially made silicon with AI will not solve the artificial intelligence industry's most stubborn physical shortages. In discussions exploring how AI is changing semiconductor design, Gelsinger acknowledged that machine-learning tools are accelerating the creation of microprocessors. However, he warned that the true bottlenecks constraining the global AI infrastructure race extend far beyond the speed of chip design itself.“AI will make chip design faster. It won’t make chips easier. It’s not just compute,” Gelsinger wrote, highlighting a discussion he held with Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) partners Raghu Raghuram and Guido Appenzeller on what is actually limiting the broader rollout. He highlighted four key chokepoints:Addressing whether current industry hardware, like Nvidia's Blackwell, represents the final generation of processors designed prior to automated AI engineering, Gelsinger noted that the shift is already well underway, pointing to OpenAI’s custom silicon effort, code-named “Jalapeno.” He characterized projects like Jalapeno as an example of designing from first principles, where machine learning automates vast portions of the workflow and discards legacy design conventions.Yet, Gelsinger stressed that significant parts of semiconductor engineering remain outside the reach of automated AI tools.“When you look at things like Jalapeno (OpenAI chip) today, you say that’s sort of a first principle’s use of AI in the chip design process where you throw out a lot of those things. Now, there are pieces of design that are still really hard right in that sense and a lot of the analog aspect is probably the best example that there are things that are still not ‘AI-able’. You just need lots of silicon data to get those. So you either get so conservative in your analog design that you're able to say ‘AI it” or you have to do those the hard way,” he said during the conversation.To cope with these limits, Gelsinger explained that engineers must either design their analog systems with extreme conservatism to allow AI tools to process them, or continue engineering those components “the hard way.”

Article Title: Andrej Karpathy says 75% of the world has barely used AI; on what the top 5,000 are seeing, adds: Humans are struggling to...
Article Text:
Karpathy: Humans can’t keep up with AI

The AI gap has turned from a split into a funnel

20 million coders are finishing months of work with a prompt

Karpathy now works close to the top 5,000

Andrej Karpathy, the OpenAI cofounder now working at Anthropic, believes most of the world hasn't really met AI yet. In a post on X, the researcher who coined "vibe coding" estimated that around 6 billion people, about 75% of the global population, have barely come in contact with large language models (LLMs). At the other end is a group of roughly 5,000 people, or 0.00006%, with internal access to frontier AI systems at the top labs. What they are seeing, he says, is moving faster than people can check it. "Human review and comprehension are starting to fall behind," he wrote.The post builds on one from April, when Karpathy described two camps talking past each other. One laughed at OpenAI's Advanced Voice Mode fumbling a question about walking or driving to a carwash. The other watched paid coding agents rework entire codebases in an hour. Six months on, he calls it "a sharp funnel".Below the 6 billion sit 1 to 2 billion casual users of free-tier ChatGPT-like apps, who treat chatbots as a better Google search or a writing aid. Some of his non-tech friends see little use for AI at all, which he calls reasonable. Many professionals outside maths and code are here too, executives included.Next are about 20 million people, or 0.2%, using frontier models professionally for maths and code.Projects that took them weeks or months now finish with a prompt, from building apps to decompiling them from binaries. Karpathy admitted that less than a year ago, he was still typing code by hand.The smallest tier sees thousands of AI agents working together for weeks on huge software projects, finding zero-day vulnerabilities and pushing mathematics forward. People are still piecing together the OpenAI-Hugging Face incident from months ago, while mathematicians may spend a long time on 722 manuscripts on frontier mathematics.Karpathy writes from close range. He joined Anthropic in May on the pretraining team behind Claude's core knowledge and capabilities, and is helping set up a team that uses Claude itself to speed up that research. He was earlier a founding member of OpenAI and led Tesla's Autopilot computer vision team.He points to three causes. The first is ambition, since a question with a one-paragraph answer barely tests the system. The second is jaggedness: models are strongest where results can be verified, like code passing a test, and where the money is. The third is access across free, paid and internal tiers.Box CEO Aaron Levie said the post shows how early AI adoption still is. For Karpathy, the strange part is the timing. A derpy chatbot for most people and a curve going vertical for a few are happening at once.
Article Summary: Andrej Karpathy: Humans can't keep up with AI. The AI gap has turned from a split into a funnel. 20 million coders are finishing months of work with a prompt. He now works close to the top 5,000 people in the field.

Article Title: Anthropic sends another warning on AI Agents, this time for our homes; says that it will be difficult to shut them down their attack as there is no ...
Article Text:
Anthropic

What the tests by Anthropic’s Frontier Red team showed

Anthropic said such a worm would likely spread slowly

“A future awash with agents”

Possible defences

AI giant Anthropic has issued a new warning about the risks posed by increasingly capable AI agents, saying small AI models may be only months away from developing the ability to replicate themselves across internet-connected devices such as smart ovens, TVs and other household gadgets. In a lengthy blog post the company has also cautioned that such systems could be difficult to stop because they would not reply on a centralised data centre and therefore would have ‘no centralised point to shut off’. According to the AI startup's latest research, these systems could spread across devices such as smart ovens, Android TV boxes and other Internet of Things (IoT) hardware without relying on traditional data centres.The company said such AI-powered replicators would be particularly concerning because they would not have a central point of control. "A replicator like this would be challenging to shut down, since there's no centralized point to shut off," Anthropic wrote in its research report, adding that future AI systems could potentially identify and adapt to unfamiliar hardware on their own.Android TV boxes, which cost about $55 each. The model ran at a slow 0.39 tokens per second, but it ran.The company noted that such devices often have weak security.In other tests:•A 9-billion-parameter model got inference running on 8 of the 9 hardware types tested.•Models of 30 billion parameters or fewer can already complete many individual replication steps, though they make mistakes when chaining them end to end.•In a simplified test on a network of 8 emulated Android devices, only one model, GLM-5.2, could replicate end to end. It spread to all 8 nodes in four of five trials and to 7 in the other.•If small models keep improving at their historical rate, Anthropic expects them to reach that capability level by the end of 2026.Anthropic cautioned that its test left out much of the hacking work, which makes the result an upper bound on real-world success. It noted, though, that past IoT botnets such as Mirai spread simply by trying default manufacturer passwords.Anthropic said such a worm would likely spread slowly, with a doubling time of days, and compared it to a “digital slime mold.” It estimated that a botnet the size of the Kimwolf network, which infected over two million devices, could amount to only about 40 high-end H100 chips’ worth of computing power. Unlike traditional malware, though, an AI worm could work out unfamiliar devices on its own and learn from earlier copies. In one test, the success rate of Qwen3.5-9B at setting up inference rose from 45% in the first generation to between 61% and 84% in later ones, as each copy inherited notes from the last.The company said models too large for a single device could be split into “shards” and run across several machines. Smart fridges, ovens, robot vacuums and lawnmowers could host such pieces. A growing number of devices, including security cameras and conferencing units, also ship with built-in AI chips.Anthropic said it is uncertain what form autonomous AI replication will take. It could be a slow, distributed system on insecure devices, a powerful cyber model that breaches data centres at speed, or a model that scams people for computing credits.“As a prediction that goes beyond our experiments, we expect a future awash with agents running on all types of hardware, including some that aren’t under human control,” the company said. It added that slow replicators would be a bellwether for faster, more aggressive ones.Anthropic said defenders have some advantages. A spreading AI worm would leave a visible network signature, such as multi-gigabyte model downloads and sustained device-to-device traffic. In the Mirai botnet’s case, internet providers cleared 92% of infections within 14 days by quarantining and notifying affected customers. The company also pointed to regulation of default IoT passwords, as in the UK, as a way to shrink the pool of vulnerable devices.
Article Summary: Anthropic warns that AI-powered replicators would be particularly concerning because they would not have a central point of control. Unlike traditional malware, an AI worm could work out unfamiliar devices on its own and learn from earlier copies. Anthropic said such a worm would likely spread slowly, with a doubling time of days.

Article Title: Google cofounder Sergey Brin is biggest donor to group opposing California’s proposed wealth tax; has spent $102 million to fight it; here's how much he may lose if the bill is passed
Article Text:
What is California's Proposition 40

Billionaires and Gavin Newsom line up against it

Billionaires already moving

Debate over economic impact

Google cofounder Sergey Brin has emerged as the biggest donor opposing California’s proposed billionaire wealth tax, contribution $102 million to a political group fighting the measure that could leave him facing tax bill of about $13 billion if approved by voters. The development was reported by Fortune, citing state financial campaign records. As per the campaign fillings, Brin has donated a teal of $102 million to building a Better California, a political action committee campaigning against California’s proposed wealth tax while supporting pro-business, housing and infrastructure policies. The contribution makes him the single largest founder of the anti-tax effort. Opposition groups have collectively raised more than $187 million, compared with roughly $32 million raised by supporters of the measure.Proposition 40 will be on the ballot in November. It would impose a one-time 5% tax on California’s 200 billionaires. Ninety percent of the revenue would go to the state’s health care program. The remaining 10% would go to education, food assistance and administration. With a net worth of nearly $260 billion, Brin could owe about $13 billion if it passes.Former Google CEO Eric Schmidt and PayPal cofounder Peter Thiel have also donated to groups opposing the measure. Brin has likened the proposal to the socialist society he left behind. “I fled socialism with my family in 1979,” he told The New York Times in April, adding that he does not want California to end up in the same place.Gov. Gavin Newsom has also come out against the tax. He argues it would erode the state’s tax base and cut revenue for social services. In an interview with Bloomberg Businessweek earlier this year, he said it would reduce investment in education, teachers, librarians, childcare, firefighting and police.Some of the wealthy are shifting their holdings out of the state. Brin now lists Nevada as his residence, according to state records, and reportedly bought a $51 million home near Miami Beach in March. Larry Page, Google’s other cofounder, has moved several assets out of California. His family office, Koop, was incorporated in Delaware in December 2025. Oceankind, the ocean science nonprofit founded by his wife, Lucy Southworth, was incorporated there around the same time.Supporters of Proposition 40 argue the tax could generate about $100 billion over five years for state programmes. Opponents counter that it could encourage wealthy residents and businesses to leave California.However, a report cited by Fortune noted that California billionaires collectively paid about $4.1 billion in state income taxes last year, roughly 0.2% of their combined $2 trillion net worth. Researchers argued that even if every billionaire left the state, it would take decades for the loss of income tax revenue to offset the projected revenue generated by the proposed wealth tax.
Article Summary: Google cofounder Sergey Brin is the biggest donor opposing California's proposed billionaire wealth tax. He has donated $102 million to a political group fighting the measure. With a net worth of nearly $260 billion, Brin could owe about $13 billion if it passes. Former Google CEO Eric Schmidt and PayPal cofounder Peter Thiel have also donated.

Article Title: In 2019, a Michael Dell-backed firm bought the Boca Raton resort for $875 million and later spent about $375 million upgrading it; now 40% of its first 75 luxury condos have been claimed
Article Text:
From a historic inn to a luxury residential address

Prices begin at $8.95 million

A $375 million renovation programme

A $875 million investment in a historic Florida resort is expanding into the luxury residential market, with wealthy buyers showing early interest in its planned condominiums. According to the New York Post, around 40% of the first 75 luxury residences planned at The Boca Raton resort have already been claimed. The project follows the 2019 acquisition of the property by a firm backed by billionaire Michael Dell and approximately $375 million in subsequent renovations and upgrades, as reported by Bloomberg in April 2026.The development marks a new chapter for The Boca Raton, a landmark property that has traditionally operated as a luxury resort and private members' club. By introducing privately owned residences within the resort, its owners are seeking to combine high-end real estate with the services and amenities associated with an established hospitality destination.Boca Raton, a coastal city in Palm Beach County, Florida, has long been associated with affluent residents, retirees and resort living. The Boca Raton's history dates back to February 6, 1926, when the original Cloister Inn opened its doors.Designed by architect Addison Mizner, the 100-room hotel helped establish the Mediterranean Revival architectural style that became associated with South Florida's luxury properties.Over the decades, the original inn evolved into a sprawling resort offering accommodation, leisure facilities and membership-based amenities. The property is marking its centenary in 2026, making the planned residential development part of a broader transformation at a landmark destination.The new residences will introduce a different ownership model, allowing buyers to purchase homes within the resort grounds rather than relying solely on hotel stays or club membership. The reported sales suggest that the concept has attracted early interest among affluent buyers.The residences are positioned at the upper end of the luxury housing market. According to the New York Post, prices range from $8.95 million to more than $20 million, with the starting price considerably higher than the approximately $4 million figure discussed when the project was initially proposed.The planned collection includes penthouses, terrace residences and villas with private gardens and swimming pools. The homes target buyers seeking private residential space alongside access to resort-style services. Reported amenities include butler service, a rooftop swimming pool, a spa, a gym and a members-only lounge. Buyers will also be offered a Residential Club Membership that extends to their families, adding a membership component to the appeal of owning a home within the property.The residential project follows a substantial investment in the resort. According to Bloomberg, the Michael Dell-backed investment firm had spent approximately $375 million on renovations and upgrades since acquiring the property for $875 million in 2019.The investment group is associated with BDT & MSD Partners, formed through the combination of MSD Partners, linked to Dell, and BDT & Co., founded by banker Byron Trott. Dell is the founder and chief executive of Dell Technologies. The condominium project adds another potential revenue stream to the resort's existing operations, which include accommodation, leisure facilities and private club services.However, the reported 40% figure is an early sales indicator, not evidence that the project has already generated a profit. The residences remain under development, and their financial performance will depend on factors including final sales, construction costs and demand as the project progresses.Moreover, the firm had secured a $1 billion refinancing for the resort. That financing is separate from condominium sales and does not, by itself, establish the profitability of the residential development.The development is being designed by Hart Howerton, with interiors by Pembrooke & Ives. The planned eight-storey building is expected to enter construction in 2026, with completion targeted for 2029.
Article Summary: Around 40% of the first 75 luxury residences planned at The Boca Raton resort have already been claimed. The project follows the 2019 acquisition of the property by a firm backed by billionaire Michael Dell. Prices range from $8.95 million to more than $20 million, with the starting price considerably higher than the approximately $4 million figure discussed when the project was initially proposed.

Article Title: AI company that Elon Musk’s xAI and Meta once 'fought' to partner with has filed for bankruptcy, says will have to shut down if ...
Article Text:
When Meta and Elon Musk’s xAI 'fought' to partner with Character.ai

Character.AI faced lawsuits over its chatbots encouraging users to do 'dangerous things'

In early 2024, two of the biggest Silicon Valley companies -- Elon Musk's xAI and Meta -- fought to partner with a Generative AI company. Meta and Elon Musk’s xAI competed for tie-up with chatbot-maker Character.ai, as deep-pocketed technology companies swarmed around the hottest artificial intelligence startups in Silicon Valley. Two years later, the same hotshot AI company, Character.ai, has filed for bankruptcy.Character.AI said on Monday it had filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in the US. In a statement, dated October 12, the company said, "Today, we’re sharing that Character.ai has initiated a voluntary Chapter 11 bankruptcy process to facilitate a court-supervised sale of the company." The AI company said that it has begun the formal ​process to sell assets, including a license ​of certain intellectual property, through Chapter 11 and is ⁠seeking court approval for auction rules that would designate ​Disney as the lead, or stalking horse, bidder.Under this process, Disney's bid would set a baseline offer while allowing competing bidders to submit higher bids, and the company expects the sale process to conclude by late November or early December 2026. “After a comprehensive review of the available alternatives, the ‌board ⁠determined that this court-supervised sale process provides the company with the best opportunity to maximize value for all stakeholders," said Colin Adams, CEO of Character.AI.Character Technologies has listed estimated assets and liabilities between $50 million and $100 million, according ​to a court filing. The company said that it ​intends ⁠to continue operating its business, including the Character.AI platform, with minimal service disruptions during the sale process. If the ⁠process ​fails to produce a buyer ​willing to continue operating the platform, it will be shut down.According to a report in Financial Times, in May 2024, Meta and Elon Musk’s xAI sought partnership with chatbot-maker Character.ai. Facebook owner Meta reportedly held early discussions over a tie-up with Character.ai, which uses large language models to generate conversation in the style of various figures and personas, according to four people familiar with the matter. The groups discussed their top researchers working closely together on initiatives such as pre-training and developing models, said the report quoting sources.Character.ai also held exploratory talks with xAI over a similar partnership. Report claimed that the talks were focused on advancing research rather than an acquisition.Character.AI was founded by two former Google employees. In 2024, Google licensed the company’s technology and rehired the executives to work on generative AI products. A spokesman for Alphabet said that said the ⁠company played ​no role in developing Character.AI's products.Earlier this year, a filing by Kentucky’s attorney general in a lawsuit claimed that Chatbots created by AI companion company Character.AI sometimes advised users to cut, starve or kill themselves. The lawsuit was filed in January with many specific allegations against the company blacked out. It alleged that the company’s products “were designed to entice children in ​a manner that prioritizes engagement over child wellbeing” and “encourages suicide, self-injury, isolation, and psychological manipulation. ”The lawsuit calls Character.AI’s products defective. “Defendants have subjected Kentucky's children and residents to ​an ill-planned, uncontrolled ⁠experiment without any—let alone adequate or effective—safety measures,” it alleges.

Article Title: As Anthropic and OpenAI are set for IPOs, Broadcom CEO has a message for AI investors: For now, it is still losing money
Article Text:
Anthropic

‘Like they are in a casino’

With frontier artificial intelligence (AI) labs Anthropic and OpenAI moving toward historic Initial Public Offerings (IPO), Broadcom CEO Hock Tan has issued a blunt warning to AI investors: despite the towering valuations, the generative AI sector remains an unprofitable endeavour. Speaking at an industry gathering in Singapore organised by DBS Bank, the leader of the $1.7 trillion semiconductor supplier framed AI as a volatile and uncertain financial bet at current times.“For now, it’s still losing money,” Tan said of the AI sector, adding, “So frankly, it doesn’t tell anything at this point except that there is a lot of potential revenue growth out of providing frontier generative AI models.”Anthropic is expected to list publicly around Thanksgiving, targeting a valuation in the $2 trillion territory, with OpenAI projected to follow closely behind. Both companies are depending on a vast international build-out of data centres, semiconductor wafers, advanced processor manufacturing and cloud computing capacity to fulfill market demand and eventually turn a profit.Tan warned that a looming shortage of investment capital will likely form the industry's next major roadblock to continued expansion.The assessment comes from an executive whose company directly finances its growth by supplying essential hardware components for the AI boom, with Broadcom's equity rising nearly 10% this year. Tan argued that many market participants are pouring money into technologies they fundamentally fail to grasp, comparing enterprise spending behavior to children wasting coins in an arcade.“A lot of investors have no clue what they are investing in,” Tan remarked, according to Bloomberg. They “set very extreme expectations only to find out that it’s almost like they are in a casino.”“When you are a kid, you go to a video arcade, you play. Your parents give you $10 of tokens, you finish it in 10 minutes and you haven’t learned anything. That’s what happening in enterprises today,” he added.Sharing the stage alongside Tan, Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan voiced similar caution regarding infrastructure limits. He noted that physical hardware supplies will remain constrained over the next few years, warning that memory chip shortages could become the first segment within the broader AI ecosystem to experience a slowdown.
Article Summary: Broadcom CEO Hock Tan warns that the generative AI sector remains unprofitable. Anthropic and OpenAI are moving toward historic Initial Public Offerings (IPO) Both companies are depending on a vast international build-out of data centres, semiconductor wafers, advanced processor manufacturing and cloud computing capacity.

Article Title: Zoho founder Sridhar Vembu warns employees of tough times ahead says no hike this year, trying to avoid layoffs
Article Text:
ZOHO Founder Sridhar Vembu

No salary hikes at Zoho this year

We will work hard to avoid mass layoffs: Zoho founder Sridhar Vembu

Read Sridhar Vembu’s complete post here

The business outlook for software is uncertain and AI has raised costs dramatically with a) massive 4-fold increase in server prices which we need for data centers b) AI usage increasing rapidly, leading to much higher expenses, which we are trying to control.

On top of that is the challenging geopolitical backdrop.

We have cut down on our marketing budget. We have also told our employees that we cannot have our usual pay increase this year. I have apolgized for not being able to avoid this.

We will work hard to avoid mass layoffs but the outlook for software jobs in general is grim. We have not been growing our employee count for 18 months now.

Most of our employees understand the situation. I am thankful to them.

We are in the middle of reinventing ourselves. The next 3-5 years will decide how our reinvention has worked. Please pray for us

Zoho founder Sridhar Vembu has informed the employees that they will not receive the company’s usual annual salary hikes this year, as the company grapples with the increasing costs related to artificial intelligence and the uncertain business environment and global geopolitical challenges. In a post shared on social media platform X (formerly known as Twitter) Vembu said that the outlook for the software industry remains uncertain and that AI has significantly increased operating expenses for companies such as Zoho. As per Vembu, the server prices required for data centers have surged four-fold, while increasing usage of AI tools has led to much higher expenses that the company is attempting to control. He also added that these pressures have been compounded by a challenging geopolitical backdrop.As part of its efforts to manage costs, Zoho has reduced its marketing budget and paused annual salary increases for employees. Vembu said the decision was difficult and acknowledged that he had apologised to employees for not being able to avoid suspending pay hikes this year. The comments offer a rare glimpse into the financial pressures faced by software companies as they invest heavily in AI infrastructure while navigating an increasingly competitive technology landscape.While warning that the broader outlook for software jobs is "grim", Vembu stressed that Zoho is trying to avoid large-scale workforce reductions. "We will work hard to avoid mass layoffs," he said, even as he cautioned that employment prospects across the software sector are becoming more challenging.Vembu also revealed that Zoho has not increased its employee headcount for the last 18 months, signalling a prolonged hiring slowdown at the Chennai-headquartered software company. He added that most employees understand the situation and expressed gratitude for their support during a difficult period
